channel.title: All-Style
channel.description: All-Style is the Style Atlas: every named style in fashion, interiors, hair, beauty and occasions explained, plus free tools that tell you which styles are yours and match you with a pro.

item.title: Old Money: Inherited-looking elegance: logo-free, beautifully made, never in a hurry.
item.description: Old Money dresses like the clothes were bought decades ago and cared for ever since. Quality fabrics, neutral colours and conservative cuts do the talking; logos, trends and visible effort are avoided. It overlaps with what the internet calls quiet luxury.

item.title: Minimalist: Fewer pieces, cleaner lines, more outfits.
item.description: Minimalist fashion strips an outfit to clean silhouettes, a tight palette and excellent fit. A small wardrobe of interchangeable basics replaces trend pieces, so every item works with almost every other.

item.title: Classic: The pieces that have worked for 70 years and will work for 70 more.
item.description: Classic style relies on garments whose shapes barely change: trench coats, white shirts, straight jeans, little black dresses and tailored jackets. It is less about a mood and more about reliability: everything fits, everything matches.

item.title: Streetwear: Sneaker culture, graphic layers and limited drops.
item.description: Streetwear mixes skate, hip-hop and sportswear codes into oversized, graphic-led outfits. Sneakers anchor the look and scarcity (drops, collaborations) drives desire.

item.title: Bohemian: Free-spirited layers, prints and natural textures.
item.description: Boho fashion layers flowing silhouettes, earthy prints and handcrafted accessories. It feels relaxed, romantic and well-travelled, mixing vintage, folk and festival references.

item.title: Dark Academia: Tweed, books and candlelit libraries.
item.description: Dark Academia borrows the uniform of an old university: tweed, wool, plaid and loafers in deep, moody colours. It is as much about mood (studying, poetry, old buildings) as about clothes.

item.title: Light Academia: Dark Academia's sunnier sibling: linen, cream and poetry in the park.
item.description: Light Academia keeps the scholarly references but swaps the moody palette for cream, beige and soft brown. Linen, cotton and loose knits make it airy and optimistic.

item.title: Cottagecore: Pastoral romance: florals, puff sleeves and homemade bread.
item.description: Cottagecore idealises a slow countryside life. Prairie dresses, florals, aprons and natural fabrics evoke gardens, baking and handcraft.

item.title: Y2K: Low-rise, baby tees and shiny everything: the 2000s, remixed.
item.description: Y2K revives turn-of-the-millennium fashion: low-rise jeans, baby tees, butterfly clips, tinted sunglasses and metallics. It is playful, a little kitsch and pop-culture driven.

item.title: Grunge: Flannel, combat boots and a deliberate lack of polish.
item.description: Grunge is anti-fashion: worn flannel, ripped denim, band tees and boots layered with an undone attitude. The point is comfort and rebellion rather than perfection.

item.title: Preppy: Polos, chinos and boat shoes: campus-classic and crisp.
item.description: Preppy style comes from American prep schools and Ivy League campuses: polos, Oxford shirts, chinos, cable knits and blazers in clean, cheerful colours. It is tidy, sporty and optimistic.

item.title: Coastal Grandmother: Linen, sea air and a farmers'-market tote.
item.description: Coastal Grandmother is breezy, comfortable luxury: white linen, cashmere throws, striped tops and wide-brim hats, as if you live in a beach house and cook every evening.

item.title: Scandi Style: Functional minimalism with a playful Copenhagen twist.
item.description: Scandi style combines practical, high-quality basics with relaxed silhouettes and occasional bold colour or print. It is designed for bikes, rain and real life, yet always looks considered.

item.title: Athleisure: Gym-ready pieces styled for everything else.
item.description: Athleisure wears performance fabrics outside the gym: leggings, joggers, technical layers and sneakers styled with polished pieces like blazers or long coats.

item.title: Gorpcore: Technical outdoor gear worn in the city.
item.description: Gorpcore turns hiking and climbing gear into street style: fleeces, shell jackets, trail shoes and utility pants in earthy or bright technical colours.

item.title: Business Casual: Professional without the full suit.
item.description: Business casual blends tailored pieces with relaxed ones: trousers or skirts with knitwear, shirts or blouses, and smart shoes. It signals competence while staying comfortable for long days.

item.title: Clean Girl: Slick bun, glowing skin, gold hoops, effortless basics.
item.description: The Clean Girl aesthetic is about looking fresh and put-together with minimal effort: slicked-back hair, dewy skin, simple gold jewellery and neutral, fitted basics.

item.title: Coquette: Bows, lace and pale pink with a knowing wink.
item.description: Coquette leans into hyper-feminine details: ribbons, lace, ballet flats, pearls and soft pastels. It is romantic, girlish and nostalgic, often mixing vintage lingerie-inspired pieces with everyday basics.

item.title: Western: Cowboy boots, denim and turquoise, styled for the city.
item.description: Western style takes ranch and rodeo staples (boots, denim, fringe, big buckles and turquoise) and wears them as fashion. It ranges from rugged to glamorous.

item.title: Techwear: Black, waterproof, strapped and ready for the city of the future.
item.description: Techwear combines performance fabrics with utilitarian design: waterproof shells, cargo pants with straps and buckles, and a mostly black palette. Function and a futuristic look matter equally.

item.title: Parisian Chic: Effortless, a little undone and always flattering.
item.description: Parisian chic is a few perfect basics worn with confidence: a Breton top, straight jeans, a trench, ballet flats and red lipstick. It looks unplanned but relies on fit and restraint.

item.title: Mob Wife: Faux fur, leopard print, gold and unapologetic glamour.
item.description: The Mob Wife aesthetic is loud luxury: big faux-fur coats, animal print, black leather, oversized sunglasses and chunky gold. It is the opposite of quiet luxury.

item.title: Sprezzatura (Italian Menswear): Tailored menswear worn with studied nonchalance.
item.description: Sprezzatura is the Italian art of making great tailoring look effortless: soft jackets, open collars, rolled sleeves and a slightly imperfect tie. It rewards fit, texture and confidence.

item.title: Japandi: Japanese calm meets Scandinavian warmth.
item.description: Japandi blends Japanese minimalism and wabi-sabi with Scandinavian comfort and function. Low furniture, natural wood, muted earth tones and very little clutter create rooms that feel quiet and grounded.

item.title: Mid-Century Modern: 1950s optimism: tapered legs, teak and clean lines.
item.description: Mid-Century Modern furniture is defined by organic and geometric shapes, tapered wooden legs, moulded plywood and a mix of warm woods with pops of mustard, teal or orange. It feels both retro and surprisingly current.

item.title: Scandinavian: Light, simple, cosy: designed for long dark winters.
item.description: Scandinavian interiors use white or pale walls, light wood floors, simple functional furniture and soft textiles to maximise light and comfort. Hygge (cosiness) is the emotional core.

item.title: Modern Farmhouse: Rustic warmth with crisp, modern lines.
item.description: Modern Farmhouse pairs rustic elements (shiplap, reclaimed wood, barn doors) with clean, contemporary furniture and black metal accents in a mostly white and neutral scheme.

item.title: Industrial: Exposed brick, raw metal and loft-sized drama.
item.description: Industrial interiors celebrate raw structure: exposed brick, ductwork and concrete, paired with metal and reclaimed wood furniture and Edison-bulb lighting.

item.title: Bohemian Interior: Plants, pattern and layered global textiles.
item.description: Bohemian interiors layer rugs, textiles, plants and collected objects from different cultures and eras. The result is relaxed, colourful and personal.

item.title: Coastal: Breezy whites, sandy neutrals and ocean blues.
item.description: Coastal interiors feel like a beach house: airy whites, sandy neutrals, soft blues, natural fibres and lots of light. Modern versions skip the anchors and shells for texture and calm.

item.title: Minimalist Interior: Less, but better: space as the main material.
item.description: Minimalist interiors reduce furniture and decor to the essentials, using clean lines, a restrained palette and generous empty space. Every object is chosen for function or meaning.

item.title: Art Deco: Jazz Age glamour: geometry, brass and velvet.
item.description: Art Deco is glamorous and geometric: symmetrical patterns, fan shapes, brass and gold metals, lacquer, velvet and bold contrasts like black and gold or emerald and cream.

item.title: Traditional: Heirlooms, symmetry and rich wood.
item.description: Traditional interiors draw on 18th- and 19th-century European design: dark woods, symmetry, detailed mouldings, rich fabrics and patterns like florals and damask.

item.title: Transitional: The sweet spot between traditional and contemporary.
item.description: Transitional design blends traditional comfort with modern simplicity: classic shapes stripped of ornament, neutral palettes and a mix of wood, metal and soft fabrics.

item.title: Contemporary: What designers are doing now: sculptural, open and current.
item.description: Contemporary design means current design, so it evolves. Today it features sculptural furniture, curved shapes, open space, neutral bases and statement lighting or art.

item.title: Modern Organic: Warm minimalism: curves, wood and natural texture.
item.description: Modern Organic combines minimalist layouts with natural materials, soft curves and warm neutrals. Think limewash walls, bouclé, travertine and sculptural wood.

item.title: Wabi-Sabi: Beauty in imperfection, age and simplicity.
item.description: Wabi-Sabi embraces the imperfect and impermanent: handmade ceramics, raw plaster, worn wood and natural fibres in earthy tones. It values patina, quiet and authenticity.

item.title: Maximalist: More is more: colour, pattern and personality.
item.description: Maximalism layers bold colour, clashing patterns, art and collections to create rooms full of personality. Done well, a strong palette and repeated motifs hold the chaos together.

item.title: Mediterranean: Sun-washed plaster, terracotta and arches.
item.description: Mediterranean interiors evoke southern Europe: textured white or ochre walls, arches, terracotta tiles, wrought iron, wood beams and sea-blue accents.

item.title: Hollywood Regency: Old Hollywood glamour, high contrast and high shine.
item.description: Hollywood Regency is theatrical luxury: lacquered and mirrored furniture, velvet, bold colours, gold accents and high-contrast patterns like black-and-white stripes.

item.title: French Country: Provençal charm: toile, curved wood and faded elegance.
item.description: French Country mixes rustic farmhouse comfort with refined French details: curved painted furniture, toile and gingham fabrics, linen, and soft colours like lavender, butter yellow and blue.

item.title: Biophilic: Nature-led rooms for better wellbeing.
item.description: Biophilic design connects people with nature indoors through plants, natural light, natural materials, water and organic patterns. It is linked with lower stress and better focus.

item.title: Grandmillennial: Granny chic, made fresh: chintz, wicker and scalloped edges.
item.description: Grandmillennial reworks grandmother-era decor (chintz, needlepoint, ruffled lampshades, wicker, blue-and-white porcelain) with a fresh, youthful eye and a lot of pattern.

item.title: Rustic: Rough-hewn wood, stone and fireside comfort.
item.description: Rustic interiors celebrate raw, natural materials: rough wood beams, stone fireplaces, leather and wool, in warm earthy colours. It feels like a mountain cabin.

item.title: Wolf Cut: A shaggy, choppy hybrid of the shag and the mullet.
item.description: The wolf cut has heavy, choppy layers on top and around the crown that thin out toward longer ends, giving volume and a wild, textured shape. It suits wavy and straight hair and works for any gender.

item.title: Curtain Bangs: A soft, centre-parted fringe that frames the face.
item.description: Curtain bangs are longer at the sides and shorter in the middle, parted down the centre so they sweep away like curtains. They soften features and grow out gracefully.

item.title: Bob: The chin-length classic, from blunt to French.
item.description: A bob is cut around the jaw to the shoulders, usually with little layering. Variations include the blunt bob, the French bob (with a fringe, cheekbone to jaw length) and the long bob or 'lob'.

item.title: Pixie Cut: Short, bold and low-maintenance.
item.description: A pixie is a short cut, usually shorter at the back and sides with slightly longer pieces on top, often with a side-swept fringe. It shows off bone structure and dries in minutes.

item.title: Shag: Layered, feathery and full of movement.
item.description: The shag uses many choppy layers throughout to create volume at the crown and lightness at the ends. Modern shags are softer and pair beautifully with curtain bangs.

item.title: Butterfly Cut: Short face-framing layers that give long hair a bouncy blowout look.
item.description: The butterfly cut stacks shorter, face-framing layers over long hair so it looks like a short layered cut from the front and long from the back. It creates volume and a 90s blowout effect.

item.title: Taper Fade: Clean gradient sides that keep any top style sharp.
item.description: A taper fade gradually shortens the hair at the sideburns and nape, leaving the rest longer. Low tapers are subtle and office-friendly; higher fades are bolder.

item.title: Textured Crop: Short, choppy top with a short fringe: low effort, modern shape.
item.description: The textured crop keeps hair short with a choppy, textured top pushed forward into a short fringe, usually with faded or tapered sides. It hides a receding hairline well and takes seconds to style.

item.title: Buzz Cut: The ultimate minimal haircut: one clipper guard, zero fuss.
item.description: A buzz cut is clipped short all over with clippers, sometimes with a slightly longer top (crew cut). It highlights facial features and costs almost nothing to maintain.

item.title: No-Makeup Makeup: Your skin, but better: glow, brows and a tint.
item.description: No-makeup makeup enhances rather than covers: skin tints, concealer only where needed, groomed brows, cream blush and a tinted balm. Skincare is the foundation.

item.title: Soft Glam: Polished, camera-ready makeup in diffused neutrals.
item.description: Soft glam is full makeup without harsh lines: blended neutral eyeshadow, softly sculpted cheeks, fluffy lashes and a nude or rosy lip. It photographs beautifully and suits events.

item.title: White Tie: The most formal dress code there is.
item.description: White tie is reserved for state dinners, royal events and some galas and balls. Men wear a black tailcoat, white piqué waistcoat and bow tie; women wear floor-length evening gowns, often with long gloves.

item.title: Black Tie: Evening formal: tuxedos and gowns.
item.description: Black tie means a dinner jacket (tuxedo) with a black bow tie for men, and a floor-length gown or very elegant cocktail-length dress for women. 'Black tie optional' allows a dark suit instead.

item.title: Cocktail Attire: Dressy, festive and knee-to-midi length.
item.description: Cocktail attire sits between black tie and business: suits (ties optional at many events) for men, and knee-to-midi dresses, dressy jumpsuits or elegant separates for women. It allows more colour and personality.

item.title: Business Formal: Suits, ties and the most conservative workwear.
item.description: Business formal means a dark, matching suit with a dress shirt and tie, or a tailored suit, sheath dress or skirt suit with closed shoes. It's for interviews, boardrooms, court and formal client meetings.

item.title: Smart Casual: Relaxed, but clearly made an effort.
item.description: Smart casual pairs relaxed items with sharper ones: chinos or dark jeans with a blazer or knit, a blouse with tailored trousers, clean leather sneakers or loafers. It's the most common (and most confusing) dress code.

item.title: Festive Attire: Cocktail attire with sparkle, colour and seasonal fun.
item.description: Festive attire invites guests to bring colour, sequins, velvet and playful accessories to holiday and celebration events, usually at cocktail level of formality.

item.title: Boho Wedding: Free-spirited weddings: pampas, macramé and golden hour.
item.description: A boho wedding favours relaxed outdoor settings, flowing dresses, dried and wild flowers, macramé, rugs and lanterns, with an earthy palette and a laid-back timeline.

item.title: Classic Elegant Wedding: Timeless ballroom romance: white florals, candlelight and black tie.
item.description: A classic elegant wedding uses a formal venue, white and green florals, candlelight, fine linens and a structured timeline, often with a black-tie dress code.

item.title: Rustic Barn Wedding: Country charm: wood, string lights and wildflowers.
item.description: A rustic barn wedding is set in a barn or farm, decorated with wood, burlap or linen, string lights, wildflowers and family-style dining. It feels warm and community-focused.

item.title: Modern Minimalist Wedding: Clean lines, gallery venues and statement simplicity.
item.description: A modern minimalist wedding uses architectural venues, a restrained palette, sculptural florals, clean typography and sleek attire. Every detail is intentional.
